changes: Port native trivial copyAssign via a raw-to-raw overlap-safe ptr::copy engine; zero count accepts null pointers.
Share the engine with pre-existing safe trivial assignment/copy methods and new raw-source compatibility methods.
Read internal source slices before replacing owned or borrowed storage; assign bounds and shape only after copying.
Project the stored borrowed slice with &raw mut, avoiding the full unique slice reborrow that invalidated previous raw pointers.
Validate Array2 shape and actual underlying flat length before copying; explicitly reject overflow/negative Rust extents before pointer access.

rejected_experiments.classification: invalid caller provenance, not an implementation parity failure
rejected_experiments.reason: Taking a raw pointer from a buffer and then constructing an overlapping mutable slice invalidated that pointer. This unsupported construction protocol is not in the final suite.

rejected_experiments.classification: implementation pointer projection defect fixed in candidate
rejected_experiments.reason: Calling slice::as_mut_ptr for the stored borrowed slice introduced a unique function-entry retag and invalidated a previous raw source pointer. Direct &raw mut projection now passes the unchanged same-pointer receiver test.

limitations: Public native Assign/CopyValues on arbitrary independently constructed overlapping array wrappers remains open; a protected raw buffer helper does not close that wrapper construction domain.
Raw receiver methods require valid provenance that survives their call. Deriving a pointer and then creating a competing mutable slice is not supported.
Nontrivial native forward copy-assignment aliases and const-reference writable buffer constructors remain open.
Shared Rust views still detach on mutable access; native const-cast writable aliases are not reproduced by that safe extension.

Rust Copy is an explicit native trivial-copy policy, not automatic C++ trait equivalence. Native allocator accounting, generic ABI, uninitialized values, allocation failure, and C++ exception/noexcept behavior are not proven.
Dimension overflow and invalid negative ranges are checked Rust extensions; they are not parity claims for undefined native inputs.
Native original tests were rerun and name-joined without changing any assertions; supplemental tests add no original legacy declaration credit.
